---
title: "Stream your first reply from a plugin"
sidebarTitle: "Quickstart"
description: "Add Agent SDK to a Neovim plugin: take the user's adapter by name, start a session and stream a reply into a buffer."
keywords: ["quickstart", "plugin", "session", "prompt", "streaming"]
---

This page takes a plugin from nothing to a streamed reply in a buffer. The SDK owns adapters, credentials, history and the transport. Your plugin owns every buffer and window, the prompts it sends, and what it does with the replies.

<Steps>
  <Step title="Take the user's adapter as an option">
    Add one `adapter` option to your plugin's setup. It takes the name the user gave the adapter in `agent_sdk.setup()`, or a table with a name and a model:

    ```lua
    require("your_plugin").setup({ adapter = "anthropic" })
    require("your_plugin").setup({ adapter = { name = "anthropic", model = "claude-opus-5-5" } })
    ```

    API keys, URLs and adapter definitions live in the user's `agent_sdk.setup()`, so your plugin's config holds only the name and the model. Link to [Configure adapters](/configure/adapters) from your README.
  </Step>
  <Step title="Resolve the adapter">
    Resolve it when a conversation starts, not in your plugin's setup, as the user may call `agent_sdk.setup()` after yours:

    ```lua
    local sdk = require("agent_sdk")

    local adapter, err = sdk.adapter(config.adapter.name)
    if not adapter then
      return vim.notify(err, vim.log.levels.ERROR)
    end
    ```
  </Step>
  <Step title="Start a session">
    Write your handlers once. They run for every prompt in the session:

    ```lua
    local session = sdk.session({
      adapter = adapter,
      model = config.adapter.model,
      on = {
        text = function(event)
          append(buf, event.text)
        end,
        done = function(reply)
          vim.bo[buf].modifiable = false
        end,
        error = function(event)
          if not event.cancelled then
            vim.notify(event.message, vim.log.levels.ERROR)
          end
        end,
      },
    })
    ```

    `append` is your plugin's own function that writes to a buffer. `sdk.session()` returns straight away. Nothing is sent until the first prompt.
  </Step>
  <Step title="Send a prompt">
    ```lua
    session:prompt("Why was the nil check moved?")
    ```

    `text` runs for each piece of the answer as it streams, then `done` runs with the whole reply.
  </Step>
  <Step title="Close the session">
    Call `session:close()` when the conversation ends, such as when its window closes. For an ACP agent, this stops the agent's process.
  </Step>
</Steps>
